# intenter daemon

Run and manage the Intenter daemon

The daemon is the per-user process that evaluates every command and owns
the approvals and history. `intenter setup claude` registers it with launchd,
systemd (user) or the Windows Run key and starts it; the hook also starts it
lazily when it is not running. These subcommands are for looking at it and
for the rare manual restart — a stopped daemon never means "allow": Claude's
own permission prompt takes over until it is back.

## Usage

```text
intenter daemon
```

## Examples

```console
intenter daemon status
intenter daemon restart
intenter daemon run        # foreground, for debugging
```

## Subcommands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`intenter daemon install`](intenter_daemon_install.md) | Register the per-user daemon service |

| [`intenter daemon run`](intenter_daemon_run.md) | Run the daemon in the foreground |
| [`intenter daemon start`](intenter_daemon_start.md) | Start the daemon in the background |
| [`intenter daemon status`](intenter_daemon_status.md) | Show daemon state |
| [`intenter daemon stop`](intenter_daemon_stop.md) | Stop the running daemon |
| [`intenter daemon uninstall`](intenter_daemon_uninstall.md) | Unregister the per-user daemon service |
